### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. tricho-dento-osseous syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.730)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2916)

**Proposed mechanism:** DLX3 (HGNC:2916) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of ameloblast differentiation (GO:0007464); Regulation of ameloblast differentiation (GO:0007464) —LEADS_TO→ Hypomaturation-hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta (HP:0005914); DLX3 (HGNC:2916) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of odontoblast differentiation (GO:0042476); Regulation of odontoblast differentiation (GO:0042476) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal tooth morphology (HP:0000175); DLX3 (HGNC:2916) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal hair morphology (HP:0001072); DLX3 (HGNC:2916) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal bone morphology (HP:0004873). Loss-of-function mutations in DLX3 disrupt the regulation of ameloblast differentiation, leading to hypomaturation-hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta. Concurrently, these mutations also disrupt odontoblast differentiation, hair development, and bone morphology, contributing to the broader phenotype of tricho-dento-osseous syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in DLX3 that is exclusively associated with one of the diseases but not the other, or a known benign variant in gnomAD with high frequency that is implicated in either disease. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of DLX3 in amelogenesis and osteogenesis could lead to targeted therapies for dental and skeletal defects in both conditions, potentially by modulating DLX3 expression or downstream pathways.
